overview: Thirty-six question-only outputs compare three architectures and four settings per question, followed by two voice-conversion controls. Model and setting selection uses independently decoded wording, followed by voice similarity to a separate original utterance. All nine selected processed WAVs have zero normalized Parakeet WER. The chosen examples preserve all original context PCM samples; a full local replay injects three F5 questions on a 480 ms packet timeline. F5 has the highest held-out cosine among wording-qualified variants for each question. VC lowers speaker C similarity from 0.571 to 0.496/0.403 and is excluded from the main replay.
limitations: This is a development pilot with three questions and two speakers from one meeting. ASR and speaker embeddings are proxies: they do not prove natural prosody, exact accent, perceived identity or a physical room match. The assistant inspected transcripts, timing and audio measurements; listening review is still requested from the user. Whisper-base hears Remami instead of remind me in the Chatterbox C clip while Parakeet recovers the intended words, so pronunciation remains uncertain there. Speaker C is comparatively harder. Tuning covers reference, inference and acoustic settings; model weights were not trained. No live synthesis or answer-generation result is claimed.
